question.text: An AIF's minimum capital commitment from each investor is normally INR 1 crore. But the regulation carves out reduced thresholds. Which of the following is a CORRECT reduced minimum investment under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: INR 25 lakh minimum for employees / directors of the Manager and for Accredited Investors in AI-only funds
INR 10 lakh minimum for any retail investor with CA attestation
INR 50 lakh minimum for NRIs investing via NRO account
INR 2 crore minimum for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 7: minimum investment per investor is INR 1 crore, but employees/directors of the Manager (or of AIF) may invest with a reduced floor of INR 25 lakh. Similarly, angel investors and Accredited Investors enjoy relaxed floors per the AIF (Second Amendment) 2025. **The Trap:** Option B fabricates a retail floor. Option C adds an NRI carve-out that does not exist. Option D doubles the floor for FPIs. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B test the INR 1 cr / INR 25 lakh split directly. XIX-C layers in the AI / Angel Fund nuances. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When onboarding employees of the Manager, structure their participation through a dedicated class of units — pari-passu returns with LP class but with the INR 25 lakh minimum. Document their exit on resignation carefully in the class rights section.
